6. The possible chain isomers of heptyne is/are________.
(a) 1 (b) 3 (c) 4

7. Identify the pair of position isomers of 2-methyl 1-pentene.
(a) 3-methyl 1-pentene and 2-methyl 2-pentene
(b) 3-methyl 1-pentene and 3-methyl 2-pentene
(c) 4-methyl 1-pentene and 4-methyl 2-pentene
(d) All of the above

8. Identify the aliphatic hydrocarbon with one triple bond.
(a) $\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{H}_6$ (b) $\mathrm{C}_4\mathrm{H}_8$ (c) $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_8$ (d) $\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_6$

9. The vapour density of an aliphatic unsaturated hydrocarbon 'X' is 13. Deter-
mine the number of bromine atoms required to make it saturated and iden-
tify X.

(a) 2, X → Ethane (b) 4, X → Ethene
(c) 2, X → Ethyne (d) 4, X → Ethyne

10. Identify the true statement among the following.
(a) 1-butyne and 1-pentene are homologues
(b) 1-butyne and 2-butyne are homologues
(c) 1-butene and 2-butyne are homologues
(d) 1-pentyne and 2-hexyne are homologues

11. Excess of methane, on treatment with chlorine in presence of sunlight, gives
_________ and ________.
(a) $\mathrm{CCl}_4$ and HCl (b) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Cl}$ and HCl
(c) $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ and HCl (d) $\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Cl}_2$ and HCl

12. Sodium salt of acetic acid on treatment with soda lime gives hydrocarbon
‘X’. X can also be prepared by passing a mixture of ‘Y’ and ‘Z’ over heated
nickel carbonate at 250°C Identify X, Y and Z.

(a) $\mathrm{X} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_4$, $\mathrm{Y} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_2$, $\mathrm{Z} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2$
(b) $\mathrm{X} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_4$, $\mathrm{Y} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}$, $\mathrm{Z} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$
(c) $\mathrm{X} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_4$, $\mathrm{Y} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_2$, $\mathrm{Z} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$
(d) $\mathrm{X} \rightarrow \mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4$, $\mathrm{Y} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}$, $\mathrm{Z} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$
